newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life says seeking acquisitions in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Irish Life says seeking acquisitions in U.S..

text.p: Irish Life Plc said on Thursday it was actively seeking acquisitions, with U.S. companies the most likely target.

"We remain firmly committed to expanding in the U.S. both organically and through acquisition," Managing Director David Kingston said at a news conference after the release of Irish Life's half-year results.
"In the U.S. we have invested considerable time and effort examining opportunities which might bring added value to our existing businesses," he said.
Kingston said that in the first half of 1996 Irish Life had reached the due diligence stage with two prospective acquisitions in the U.S. but had decided not to proceed.
Irish Life's embedded value earnings, the company's key profit measure, rose to 48 million punts in the first half of 1996 versus 34 million in the same period a year ago.
Embedded value earnings take into account the future value of policies sold during the year, the value of existing business and increases in shareholders' investments.
Irish Life said that although acquisitions in other areas would be considered, the U.S. was the most likely location of any takeover.

"The U.S. is the most likely area in the sense that acquisitions are available," he said. "We would have ambitions to make acquisitions elsewhere but in the Irish market and UK market it's much less predictable when acquisitions will arise."
